category: 微分方程 / 常微分方程
literal_source_claim_zh: 线性无关解的零点交错
literal_source_claim_en: The zeros of linearly independent solutions interlace.
source_attribution: Jacques Sturm, 1836 (catalog metadata only; not a source citation)
statement_blocker: The repository supplies a theorem-family gloss but no cited equation, interval, coefficient regularity, solution semantics, scalar field, nontriviality or independence convention, consecutive-zero definition, endpoint treatment, quantifier order, or exact interlacing conclusion. Beesack's inspected authoritative source distinguishes a classical compact theorem from a generalized open-interval theorem with materially different singular-endpoint cases. Selecting one without independent source admission would invent or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the interval carrier and endpoint model, real or complex scalar field, coefficient and solution function types, derivative semantics, universes, topology and normed-space structures, and every typeclass assumption.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose existence versus exact uniqueness, one-direction separation versus reciprocal separation or full interlacing, or the compact, nonsingular-endpoint, and singular-endpoint conclusion variants.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every coefficient, domain, solution, zero, endpoint, and interlacing case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the classical compact-interval theorem summarized by Beesack for continuous r,s, positive r, and (r*y')' + s*y = 0
Beesack Theorem 1(b) for two linearly independent solutions on an open interval and consecutive nonsingular zeros
the full Beesack Theorem 1 including Abel's identity, quotient monotonicity, and singular-endpoint cases
a normal-form theorem for y'' + p*y' + q*y = 0 with a checked transport to self-adjoint form
a reciprocal or globally indexed interlacing theorem derived from a one-direction exact-one statement
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, disconnected, reversed, unbounded, open, or closed interval carriers
coincident, reversed, nonconsecutive, nonisolated, or accumulating zero endpoints
zeros at a singular finite or infinite endpoint and zeros outside the equation carrier
r vanishing or changing sign and coefficients failing the source regularity conditions
the zero solution, linearly dependent solutions, common zeros, and nonsimple zeros
a reference solution with fewer than two zeros
complex-valued solutions and any order-free interpretation of interlacing
existence without uniqueness, uniqueness without the reciprocal clause, and endpoint zeros counted in the conclusion
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1384 Sturm-Liouville theory, THM-M-1385 Sturm comparison, THM-M-1387 oscillation theory, or THM-M-1388 eigenvalue problems
interlacing zeros of consecutive eigenfunctions at distinct eigenvalues presented as separation of arbitrary solutions of one fixed equation
Sturm polynomial sequences, polynomial root counting, or polynomial and matrix eigenvalue interlacing
a trigonometric example such as sine and cosine presented as the general theorem
a structure field or hypothesis that directly assumes the desired intermediate zero
generic derivative, Rolle, intermediate-value, ODE, or linear-independence infrastructure alone
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the API probe as source or proof credit
